Not every time… I—I felt the danger of having such waves, such mountains.

Nu, I was despairing; I saw the danger—what, what, what there is.

Every time there is—I see miracles; I rise over the wave, I rise over the mountain, I rise from the water.

In any case, she traveled to Yerushalayim.

And when she traveled, I said to her, “I collected money for a ‘Kol-Bo’ siddur!”

And I was very dear to my mother.

And she—she gave me a promise that she would buy me a siddur just as I wanted,

a “Kol-Bo,” that it should have—that it should have all the finest qualities, yes.

I gave her the money, and she kept her word.

And she made an effort to deal with some family, from our family, who knew all the great merchants,

because there is… such a siddur—not everywhere, not—not obtainable in every place.

One needs to know where such a siddur can be found.

In any case, she brought me a siddur that was a novelty in Yerushalayim.

She came to Teveria with the siddur, and my joy—and I went to the synagogue with this siddur.

And everyone envied me: I have—he has a siddur.

I wanted to eat the whole siddur.

What—what joy I had every time I saw the siddur with me…

…[Start from the beginning.]

I forgot.

[About the three wise men in Teveria.]

At the time he drew close—when Rav Tzvi Rosenthal drew close to Rabbainu—then Hashem, blessed is He, arranged that this was the Providence:

he left his home to pray vatikin on Friday, and did not—and did not return the whole day.

They were already waiting, the whole family—the… his wife and children and father—

waiting at every—at every moment until he would come, until he would come. How is it possible?

One goes to pray and does not return?

Nu, nu…

There was a commotion throughout the city:

“Rav Tzvi Rosenthal went to pray and… did not return.

What these Breslovers do! On Friday, Erev Shabbos, they took Rav Tzvi.

He has a wife and small children; suddenly he disappeared. Who knows where he is?”

Some said—a few people said:

“The Breslovers sent him to Uman, because the main thing for them is Uman.”

On Shabbos morning they went up—they did not come to me—to Rebbe Yisroel.

“Where is Rav Tzvi?”

I did not know. I got up, went to the mikveh, and prayed at home.

I begin to pray, “Baruch SheAmar,” and…

I—he called—called me and said, “Come to prison. Where is Rav Tzvi?”

What is this? When… Such a thing has never been heard in the world:

Such a thing—only in Breslov.

And the whole city was weeping over the family.

Rav Tzvi went to pray and did not—and did not… This can happen only—only in Breslov.
